I1.quote: High-pressure H2 (77 K) and CO2 (273 K) sorption isotherm measurements were carried out on a fully computer controlled volumetric BELSORP-HP, BEL JAPAN high pressure instrument.

I2.quote: PGFs show nearly 1.2 wt% H2 storage capacity at 77 K and 1 atm, increasing to ∼1.9 wt% at high pressure. These all carbon-based porous solids based on pillared graphene frameworks ...

I3.quote: PGF-1 and PGF-2 adsorb 1.2 and 1.0 wt% of H2, respectively, at 1 atm and 77 K (Fig. 3d).

I4.quote: The final N2 uptake was 477 mL, the application of the Brunauer–Emmet–Teller (BET) model giving a surface area of 825 m2 g−1.
I4.location: main, p. 2, main text (right column), porosity paragraph

I5.quote: We report the design and synthesis of two porous graphene frameworks (PGFs) prepared via covalent functionalization of reduced graphene oxide (RGO) with iodobenzene followed by a C–C coupling reaction.

notes: Sorbents PGF-1 and PGF-2 are reduced graphene oxide covalently pillared by hydrocarbon linkers (1,4-diethynylbenzene, 4,4'-diethynylbiphenyl); carbon is the majority component by mass and the paper calls them 'all carbon-based porous solids', so I2 is judged met (likely class reduced_graphene_oxide or composite). H2 uptake measured volumetrically: up to 1 atm at 77 and 87 K on a Quantachrome Quadrasorb-SI (si1 p. 3-4) and up to ~20 atm at 77 K on a BELSORP-HP (Fig. 4b). BET areas 825 (PGF-1) and 770 (PGF-2) m2/g, measured on the H2-tested samples. Communication with original data; no retraction or prior-publication statement found.
